pr.title: List another person's public key as a peer, from a terminal only
pr.head: 93a093bef798be7989052b4e3995d89f2f0918e0

summary: The relay currently carries messages between your own machines. This change adds the personal list of other people's public keys that a later repository-inbox layer will use; it does not yet admit their records or deliver their items.

Each peer has a local name and an X25519 public key. Only your user configuration supplies this trust list. A terminal command checks the key, asks you to confirm its ID, and writes the entry; repository configuration and the general configuration setter cannot add peers.

cards.title: Review validation
cards.html:
• The configured gate and exact-head CI passed, including 268 hook tests.
  • All 144 focused relay, configuration, and permission tests passed.
  • Both earlier findings are fixed. A temporary-state reproduction found that an overlapping addition can restore a removed peer because removal does not take the peer lock.

cards.title: This layer and the next
cards.html: The peer plan moves to in-progress. This layer stores and manages trust decisions; the relay continues to accept only the existing shared machine key until the later inbox layer uses this table.

groups.title: Read peers only from personal configuration
groups.kicker: A repository cannot add people to your trust list
intro: agent.peers is a table from names you choose to public keys. The configuration reader validates names, key lengths, duplicate identities, and the rule that your own key needs no peer entry.

The user-only filter removes each protected subtree by walking the parsed TOML tables. Quoted names containing dots stay ordinary keys, and tables emptied by filtering are removed so rejected values do not appear in configuration output.

files.note: Adds peer-table validation and recursive removal of user-only configuration from checkout layers.

checks.text: Verified that a checkout peer named "alice.work" is ignored while an unrelated configuration setting loads. The reader still obtains peers only from the user layer without reading keychain secrets.

files.note: Keeps the documented setting types aligned with the new table-valued setting.

groups.title: Manage peer trust at a terminal
groups.kicker: Confirm a key ID before recording a peer
intro: The new project agent peer commands add, list, replace, and remove peer entries. Adding requires terminal input and output and a positive confirmation of the public key's ID. Listing reports names and IDs, with public keys included in JSON output.

Validation runs before confirmation and again under the peer lock immediately before adding. This refuses a conflicting addition made while the prompt waits. Removal currently does not acquire the same lock, leaving an overlapping mutation able to restore a peer that another command removed.

files.note: Provides peer validation, personal-file mutations, and list rows; shares key-ID parsing with configuration.

checks.text: Removal does not share the add lock. An add that already read the file can overwrite a successful removal with its earlier copy, silently restoring the removed peer. Hold the same lock across removal's read, validation, and write.

files.note: Registers the peer commands, enforces terminal confirmation, and refuses general config-set additions.

checks.text: The final addition forwards --replace and revalidates after confirmation; the duplicate-key change made during the prompt is refused.

files.note: Exercises terminal refusal, confirmation, validation, replacement, removal, repository filtering, and key-display guidance.

checks.text: All 144 focused relay/configuration/permission tests passed, including the quoted-name and confirmation-window regressions. Additional reproductions used temporary configurations and synthetic keys.

groups.title: Expose the trust workflow and its limits
groups.kicker: Allow listing without allowing automatic trust additions
intro: Codex receives an explicit allow rule only for peer list; adding or removing a peer remains outside that allow rule. Permission tests and documented rules describe the same command surface.

The CLI guide explains public-key sharing and the peer table, and the project plan records that implementation has begun. The next layer must supply the repository inbox behavior that uses these trust decisions.
